questions.stem: Which set best represents an integrated safety management system rather than a collection of isolated activities?
options: Policy, risk management, assurance, and promotion operating as a connected cycle
Posters, disciplinary notices, and annual awards only
Incident rates, insurance premiums, and legal settlements only
PPE purchases, first-aid supplies, and emergency phone numbers only
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A management system links policy and accountability with risk control, assurance, communication, competence, and continual improvement.
incorrectOptionExplanations: These activities may support a program but do not form a complete management system.
These are mostly outcomes or financial measures and omit planning, control, and improvement processes.
These resources are useful but do not establish governance, risk processes, assurance, or learning.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 31, components of a safety management system, pp. 717-720

questions.stem: A safety policy promises prevention but assigns no authority, resources, or accountability. What is the most important weakness?
options: The policy should contain every work instruction
The policy is not translated into an operating governance structure
The policy should be confidential to senior management
The policy should focus only on injury-rate targets
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A credible policy must be supported by defined responsibilities, authority, resources, objectives, and accountability mechanisms.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Detailed work instructions belong in procedures and controls, not necessarily in the policy statement.
A policy must be communicated and understood to guide organizational behavior.
A narrow injury-rate focus omits prevention, compliance, participation, and continual improvement.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 31, safety policy and organizational structure, pp. 718-720

questions.stem: Which practice best demonstrates meaningful worker participation in the management system?
options: Workers receive completed procedures after management approval
Only supervisors may report hazards to the safety department
Workers help identify hazards, evaluate controls, and verify corrective actions without fear of retaliation
Participation is measured only by attendance at an annual meeting
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Meaningful participation gives workers accessible channels and a real role in identifying, controlling, and evaluating hazards.
incorrectOptionExplanations: One-way communication does not involve workers in decisions or evaluation.
Restricting reports suppresses information and weakens early hazard recognition.
Attendance alone does not show influence, feedback, or involvement in risk decisions.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 31, management systems and safety promotion, pp. 717-729

questions.stem: An organization standardizes a successful pilot control and revises system requirements based on evaluation results. Which PDCA phase is represented?
options: Plan
Do
Check
Act
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: The Act phase uses evaluation results to standardize success, correct deficiencies, and improve the management system.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Planning defines objectives and methods before implementation.
Doing implements the plan or pilot.
Checking measures results and compares them with objectives.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)

questions.stem: Which activity is primarily part of safety assurance?
options: Monitoring controls, auditing performance, and verifying that corrective actions work
Writing a broad safety vision without measures
Selecting only personal protective equipment for all hazards
Celebrating milestones without reviewing adverse trends
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Safety assurance evaluates whether the system and its controls are implemented, effective, and improving.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A vision supports policy and promotion but does not by itself verify performance.
PPE-only selection is not assurance and may bypass stronger controls.
Recognition without monitoring can overlook emerging or recurring risk.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)

questions.stem: Which action most directly supports safety promotion within a management system?
options: Limit safety information to the annual report
Provide role-specific communication, competence development, and feedback on lessons learned
Publish only favorable indicators
Replace training with a signature acknowledging policy receipt
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Safety promotion builds competence, communication, awareness, and a learning culture across the organization.
incorrectOptionExplanations: Annual-only communication is too infrequent to support ongoing awareness and learning.
Selective reporting damages trust and prevents informed improvement.
A signature does not demonstrate understanding, competence, or continuing communication.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)

questions.stem: An internal audit identifies recurring weaknesses in contractor control. What should management review add beyond the audit finding itself?
options: A second copy of the audit checklist
A requirement that the auditor implement every correction personally
A decision on system changes, resources, priorities, and accountability
Deletion of the finding after it is discussed
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Management review converts assurance information into strategic decisions, resource commitments, and direction for improvement.
incorrectOptionExplanations: A duplicate checklist adds no management decision or resource commitment.
Auditors evaluate evidence; process owners and management are accountable for corrective action.
Discussion does not resolve a finding or demonstrate effective action.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapter 31, review of safety management systems and PDCA, pp. 721-729

questions.stem: Which dashboard best supports management-system decision making?
options: Only total recordable injury rate
Only the number of safety meetings held
Only the annual workers compensation premium
A balanced set of exposure, control, participation, action-effectiveness, and outcome measures
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A balanced dashboard combines leading and lagging evidence so leaders can understand risk, implementation, effectiveness, and outcomes.
incorrectOptionExplanations: One lagging rate cannot show whether hazards and controls are changing in time to act.
Meeting count measures activity but not quality, transfer, control performance, or outcomes.
Insurance cost is influenced by multiple factors and is too indirect to manage the full system.
questions.sourceTitle: Safety Professional's Reference and Study Guide, 4th ed. (W. David Yates, CRC Press, 2025)
questions.sourceLocation: Yates Chapters 31 and 36, safety assurance and performance measurement, pp. 717-730 and 797-816
